clue.text: Offering resignation

blocks.note: first meaning: something put forward for consideration, such as an entry or proposal
second meaning: meek acceptance, yielding to another's will

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like handing in a letter of resignation; instead the two words are separate senses of one noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a thing handed over for judgement and the act of giving in or yielding.

clue.text: Put on maybe Hancock's Half Hour tapes finally, heading north

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word it follows
in a down entry, going north means climbing to the top, so the bottom letter moves up to lead

blocks.note: a ham is an overacting performer; the sitcom's hero was a pompous, hammy would-be actor, and 'maybe' marks an example
the last letter of tapes

explanation.surface: An old radio comedy series being put out again on tape.
explanation.walkthrough: Hancock's Half Hour was a 1950s BBC sitcom starring Tony Hancock. HAM followed by S gives HAMS, and the final S then climbs to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on a feeling is to fake or pretend it, which is exactly what sham means as a verb.

clue.text: Go for one willing to support committee

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece that supports another sits underneath it

blocks.note: a board is a governing committee
game means willing, as in 'game for anything'

explanation.surface: Someone eager to back a committee's proposal.
explanation.walkthrough: Go is the ancient Asian strategy game of black and white stones, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Go is a specific instance of a game played on a board, so 'for one' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Obduracy batsman ultimately lacks in a recent innings abroad

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so take only the closing letter of the word
to lack something is to be without it, so that letter is taken out of what follows
abroad suggests being scattered far and wide, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: the final letter of batsman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricketer stubbornly lacking runs in a recent innings on an overseas tour.
explanation.walkthrough: One N comes out of the fourteen letters of 'a recent innings', and the remaining thirteen are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Obduracy and intransigence are synonyms, both meaning a stubborn refusal to change one's position.

clue.text: Godfather upset crooks regularly with no afterthought

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so take every other letter of the word
in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the whole string reads from the bottom up

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of crooks
taken as written
PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter

explanation.surface: A Mafia boss angry with criminals who never think twice.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes the Mafia Godfather; the definition is the baptismal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A godfather presents a child at baptism and vouches for them, and such a person is formally called a sponsor.

clue.text: Blooming acting company is abject

blocks.note: flowers that are out are in bloom
the cast is the company of actors in a production

explanation.surface: A theatre troupe that is utterly wretched, 'blooming' used as a mild British curse.
explanation.walkthrough: Blooming looks like the British intensifier ('blooming awful'); here it is literal flowering.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, outcast describes someone rejected by society, a wretched, abject state.

clue.text: Record number gathers, returning for sports event

indicators.note: to gather something is to take it in, so one piece wraps round the other
returning means going back the way it came, so the result reads right to left

blocks.note: No. is the abbreviation for number
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A record attendance gathering for a returning sports fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: Record looks like a sporting best; here it is a vinyl disc.
explanation.definitionFit: An open is a tournament anyone may enter, such as the Open golf championship.

clue.text: Acceptable to interrupt a game?

indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks into the middle, so it sits inside the other piece

blocks.note: a and per both mean 'for each', as in fifty pence a head
OK means acceptable

explanation.surface: Is it all right to break into someone's game?
explanation.walkthrough: The tiny word 'a' is doing the heavy work: per means 'for each', just as a does in 'twice a day'.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker is a card game of betting and bluffing, so it is an instance of a game.

clue.text: Article probes North Londoner circulating anabolic steroid

indicators.note: a probe pushes inside something, so this piece goes within the other
circulating means moving round, so the letters are set moving into a new order

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for north
taken as written
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A news item investigating a North Londoner who is passing round steroids.
explanation.walkthrough: North Londoner looks like one phrase, but North supplies N to join the anagram, and A sits after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Nandrolone is a muscle-building anabolic steroid, notorious from doping cases in athletics and football.

clue.text: Norm stops heartless act alone

indicators.note: without a heart means the centre is removed, leaving only the outside letters
a stopper plugs a gap, so this piece fills the middle of the other

blocks.note: act with its middle letter gone
par is the standard or norm, as in 'up to par'

explanation.surface: Convention halts a callous deed done by a lone person.
explanation.walkthrough: Heartless and act look like an adjective and noun together; heartless is an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Apart means separately, away from others, much as alone does in 'living apart' or 'living alone'.

clue.text: Frank soon kept involved around university

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are knotted into another order
around means encircling, so the jumbled letters take in the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A man called Frank soon got caught up with a university.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a man's name; it is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone frank speaks openly and bluntly, which is the sense of the synonym outspoken.

clue.text: Old Spanish coins in wreckage from boat?

blocks.note: first meaning: silver dollars once minted in Spain, the pirates' currency
second meaning, whimsical: the broken bits of a rowing boat crewed by eight

explanation.walkthrough: An eight is a racing boat rowed by eight oarsmen, so its wreckage is literally fragments of an eight; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish silver peso, worth eight reales, was nicknamed this phrase and is famous from pirate stories.

clue.text: Spooner's asserted river could supply salt lake

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so exchange them here

blocks.note: asserted is said, pronounced 'sed', and the Dee is a British river; swap the opening sounds

explanation.surface: Spooner claims a river might provide salt for a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee flows through Wales and England, and in Scotland too.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dead Sea is a landlocked lake so salty that bathers float, a salt lake by definition.

clue.text: Fear having no time to find misprint?

indicators.note: having none of something means it is missing, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: terror is extreme fear
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A proofreader too frightened to spend time hunting for typos.
explanation.definitionFit: A misprint is a mistake in printed text, a specific kind of error.

clue.text: Purchasing restaurant, join one in business with Poles

indicators.note: purchasing something means taking it into your possession, so the next piece holds the first

blocks.note: a caff is British slang for a cheap café
to solder is to join metal with molten alloy

explanation.surface: Buying a restaurant and going into partnership with Polish business people.
explanation.walkthrough: Poles looks like people from Poland; the capital P disguises scaffolding poles.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaffolder erects scaffolding, a framework of metal poles, so the job is a trade working with poles.

clue.text: Comparatively rude individual hunting with hounds, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so the word is spelt differently from how it is said

blocks.note: a courser is one who courses, chasing hares with hounds

explanation.surface: A rather crude huntsman riding to hounds.
explanation.walkthrough: Coursing is hunting hares with dogs that follow by sight, a now-banned British field sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Coarse means crude or vulgar, so the comparative form means ruder than another.

clue.text: Current account left short when touring Channel Island

indicators.note: left short means cut off before the end, so the final letter goes
touring means travelling round, so the shortened word goes round the island

blocks.note: a tale is an account or story
Herm is one of the small Channel Islands, near Guernsey

explanation.surface: A bank's current account left in deficit during a holiday on Jersey or Guernsey.
explanation.walkthrough: Current account is the British name for a checking account; the two words are split, Current being the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A thermal is a rising current of warm air used by gliders and birds.

clue.text: Following artist Miles around, cast wink at writer

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so these letters read backwards
cast means thrown, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician
M is the abbreviation for miles
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter named Miles throws a wink at an author.
explanation.walkthrough: Miles looks like a first name, but it is the unit abbreviation. 'Following' says the jumbled letters come after the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain, pen name of Samuel Clemens, wrote Tom Sawyer and Huckleberry Finn.

clue.text: Prudence to remove separately ordinary small cargo

indicators.note: removing things separately means taking each one out from its own place

blocks.note: foresight is prudent planning for the future
O is the abbreviation for ordinary
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A woman called Prudence shifting ordinary small loads one by one.
explanation.walkthrough: Prudence looks like a woman's name; it is the quality. The O and S sit apart in the longer word, hence 'separately'.
explanation.definitionFit: Freight is goods carried by ship, train or lorry, the same thing as cargo.

clue.text: PM mostly attracting support in Guardian

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
attracting means drawing something to oneself, so the next piece attaches alongside

blocks.note: Liz Truss was briefly UK Prime Minister in 2022
a tee is a small peg supporting a golf ball

explanation.surface: A prime minister gaining backing in the pages of the Guardian newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Guardian looks like the newspaper; it is the definition, a person who looks after something.
explanation.definitionFit: A trustee holds property or affairs in trust for others, acting as their guardian.

clue.text: Soldiers right to wear period feature of Highland dress

indicators.note: something worn is put on, so the clothing piece goes round the wearer

blocks.note: a span is a period of time
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Troops correctly kitted out in historical Highland costume.
explanation.walkthrough: The dress sense of 'wear' makes it read as soldiers donning a uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporran is the pouch worn at the front of a kilt, a characteristic item of Scottish Highland costume.

clue.text: Son Oscar, out of control, departs United

indicators.note: out of means removed from, so this letter is taken from the following word

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to police something is to control it
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A wild boy named Oscar walks out on a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of control' reads as wild behaviour; it splits into an instruction plus a word. United also looks like a team name.
explanation.definitionFit: Spliced is informal for married, so a couple who are spliced have been joined or united.

clue.text: Newspaper switching focus to British politician in Hungary

indicators.note: a focus is the centre point, so the middle letter is exchanged for another

blocks.note: an organ is a newspaper or periodical voicing a group's views
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: A paper turning its attention to British politics while in Hungary.
explanation.walkthrough: The G at the centre of the five-letter word is replaced.
explanation.definitionFit: Viktor Orbán is the long-serving Hungarian prime minister, a leading politician in that country.

clue.text: Found lake somewhere in Switzerland

blocks.note: to found something is to base or establish it
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Discovered a lake on a trip through Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: Found looks like the past tense of find; it is the verb meaning establish.
explanation.definitionFit: Basel is a Swiss city on the Rhine, so it is one place within Switzerland.

clue.text: Production of glue, it's most disquieting

indicators.note: producing something means making it from raw materials, so these letters are made into a new word

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Glue manufacture is the most unsettling business there is.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition simply follows the fodder with no link; it's belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly can mean threatening or alarming, as in an ugly mood, so the superlative is most disquieting.

clue.text: Studies inside condensation

indicators.note: inside means within, so the letters are found contained in the next word

blocks.note: the letters run consecutively in the middle of the word

explanation.surface: Research into how condensation forms.
explanation.definitionFit: A den or a study is a private room for working or reading, so the plural matches.

clue.text: Gloomy Etihad club denies originally claiming its manager's retiring

indicators.note: claiming something means taking hold of it, so one piece holds the other inside
originally means at the start, so take only the opening letter
retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the whole string reads right to left

blocks.note: the Etihad Stadium is home of Manchester City football club
Pep Guardiola is City's manager; the possessive adds S
the first letter of denies

explanation.surface: A miserable Manchester City deny their manager is about to retire.
explanation.walkthrough: The Etihad Stadium is Manchester City's home ground; their manager is Pep Guardiola. The apostrophe-S of manager's supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspeptic, literally suffering indigestion, is used figuratively for someone irritable or gloomy.

clue.text: Become princess, perhaps

blocks.note: first meaning: to suit or adorn
second meaning; 'perhaps' marks an example

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an instruction to turn into a princess, which is just what Grace Kelly did.
explanation.definitionFit: To grace is to honour or adorn, like 'become' meaning suit; and Grace is the name of a famous princess.

clue.text: Feverish having month off, developing bug

indicators.note: having something off means it has been taken away, so those letters are dropped

blocks.note: febrile means feverish
Feb is the abbreviation for February

explanation.surface: Running a temperature for weeks while coming down with a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: Bug looks like an illness; it is the verb meaning annoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To bug someone is to irritate them, so it is a synonym for rile.

clue.text: End to ashes being scattered for those standing in churchyard?

indicators.note: scattering throws things in all directions, so these letters land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Scattering a person's ashes at the end of a funeral, in place of a gravestone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Those standing' sounds like mourners at a burial; the question mark signals it means the stones themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Headstones are the upright memorial slabs at the head of graves, standing in rows in a churchyard.
